name: Ireland — Irish parties
intro: compare it with Irish political parties
inclusion_note: The test includes the main national parties of Ireland: those represented in the parliament (Dáil Éireann) and those with a significant national following. Positions are the team's estimates and are open to review.
hemicycle_note: Seats in the parliament (Dáil Éireann) after the 2024 election, arranged left to right. Approximate. 174 members.

PBP–S.name: People Before Profit–Solidarity
PBP–S.priorities: Affordable housing, Public services, Military neutrality
PBP–S.description: Socialist alliance focused on housing, public services and opposition to NATO ties.

SF.name: Sinn Féin
SF.ideologies: Irish republicanism, Democratic socialism, Left-wing populism
SF.priorities: Irish unity, Affordable housing, Public healthcare
SF.description: Irish republican party seeking Irish unity, the largest opposition party, focused on housing and health.

Lab.name: Labour Party
Lab.priorities: Affordable housing, Workers' rights and wages, Public healthcare
Lab.description: Ireland's oldest party, social-democratic and pro-European.

SD.name: Social Democrats
SD.priorities: Public healthcare, Affordable housing, Climate action
SD.description: Social Democrats, a centre-left party that grew in 2024 on health and housing.

Greens.name: Green Party
Greens.description: Green Party, which governed from 2020 to 2024 and lost nearly all its seats in 2024.

Volt.name: Volt Ireland
Volt.priorities: Deeper European integration, Climate action, Digital innovation, Democratic reform
Volt.description: National chapter of Volt Europa, the first pan-European party. All chapters share one programme: a federal and more democratic EU, evidence-based policy, a market economy with a strong welfare state, and the digital and climate transitions. Volt has the same positions in every country in this test.

FF.name: Fianna Fáil
FF.priorities: Affordable housing, Competitiveness and growth, Public healthcare
FF.description: Centrist party of Taoiseach Micheál Martin, the largest in the Dáil since 2024 and in coalition with Fine Gael.

FG.name: Fine Gael
FG.priorities: Competitiveness and growth, Fiscal discipline, Deeper European integration
FG.description: Centre-right, pro-European and pro-business party, in government since 2011.

Aontú.name: Aontú
Aontú.priorities: Irish unity, Protecting life and family, Reducing immigration
Aontú.description: Republican party that combines a united Ireland with socially conservative positions, including opposition to abortion.

II.name: Independent Ireland
II.priorities: Regions and rural services, Reducing immigration, Military neutrality
II.description: Rural, right-leaning party founded by independent TDs, critical of immigration policy.
